DIRECT IMPACTS UPON THE AREA ADJACENT TO THE PROPOSAL
No issues have been presented or discussed that are highly controversial to the implementation of this proposed improvement. All parties concerned have agreed that this is a much needed improvement and should be activated at the earliest possible opportunity.
The probable impacts of the proposed improvement consist of relative changes whether positive or negative in the environmental effects, which follow under separate headings.
A. Significant Impacts on Natural Ecological, Cultural or Scenic Resources of National, State or Local Significance.
In trying to comprehend the operation of any large or small and complex natural system, such as the constituent interaction of solid surfaces with gaseous flows and liquid media, it is oftentimes necessary to back off from the mass of detail inherent in the system and take a fresh view of the system. In an approach and analysis of this type much is dependent on how the limits of the system are defined and the status of matter or constituents in it. A useful way to analyze such a system is to compare the inputs and outputs of the major components of the system as a whole and then to deduce the kinds of environmental impacts and physical processes that control the balance. The entire analysis rests with the assumption of balance between inputs and outputs, and that inputs not inherent to the defined system produce some type of change which result in outputs that are again in balance with the inputs.
Therefore, what are the definable systems that are appropriate in the environmental analysis of transportation projects and systems? Generally the definable system could be called an "Eco-system" and an ecosystem could be assigned as—a unit with definable limits with living and non-living interacting components in dynamic balance that needs a continual supply of energy. So it will be assigned.
In the environmental assessment and analysis of a transportation project or system a "brew pot" of these interacting components with definable limits are watersheds. This is especially "appropriatus" and significant in Northeastern Illinois since these limits are well defined and documented along with other interacting component data in the Hydrologic Investigations Atlases" published by the U.S. Geological Survey.
